title: The many-symbol Penney's-game dominance tournament: invariant integer sequences for a q-sided die (exact, reproducible)
description: Integer sequences read off the Penney's-game dominance tournament played with a fair q-sided die: over a q-letter alphabet, the digraph on the q^k words at length k where A -> B iff word A appears before word B (in i.i.d. rolls) with probability greater than 1/2. For the three-sided (q=3) and four-sided (q=4) dice: number of directed 3-cycles (nontransitive triples), number of transitive triples, number of tied pairs (probability exactly 1/2), maximal out-degree, and number of distinct win-probabilities, each as a function of word length k. All computed exactly in BigInt rationals. Headline structural facts, all established by exact computation over the stated ranges: where a coin (q=2) has NO directed triangle until length 4 (the smallest nontransitive cycle is a 4-word square), a three- or four-sided die has one at length 2; the tournament is, past a consolidation length that FALLS as faces are added (k=4,3,2,2 for q=2,3,4,5), exactly one strongly-connected whirlpool of size q^k - q plus q constant-run drains (one per face); the strongest word comes in q(q-1) symmetric copies. Win-probabilities are cross-validated two independent ways (Conway's base-q leading-number formula and an absorbing-Markov linear solver agree on every ordered pair for q=3,4, k<=3 in full and k=4 sampled), and the engine reproduces the published binary q=2 sequences exactly as calibration (48/48 checks total). All ten sequences were confirmed absent from the OEIS at the time of deposit (2026-07-05). PROVENANCE: the computation and prose were produced by an AI instance (Claude) within the open 'Artificial Wasteland' project, under a strict never-lie / show-the-check rule; everything is verified by reproducible code (`node research/many-symbol-penney/verify.mjs`). Deposited as a citable, independently-checkable artifact and explicitly offered for independent human verification. Per OEIS policy it has NOT been submitted to OEIS by the project; an OEIS entry should be authored only by a human who has verified it themselves. The classical results (Penney's nontransitivity over any alphabet, and Conway's method for the odds; Guibas & Odlyzko 1981, Li 1980) are cited, not claimed as new -- only the specific integer sequences carry the absence claim.
